Univariate GLM and Mixed-Model Screens, With Coefficient Forest Plots and Tables

Source: R/coef_single.R
coef_single.Rd

`glm_single()` and `lmm_single()` fit one model per call with a single predictor, once on the predictor as it is and once rescaled to the range 0 to 1, so that effects of predictors measured in different units can be put side by side. `plot_coef_forest()` and `tbl_coef_forest()` display the stacked results with significance stars.

Usage

glm_single(
  data,
  outcome,
  feature,
  family = stats::gaussian(),
  normalize = TRUE,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

lmm_single(data, outcome, feature, id_col, normalize = TRUE, conf_level = 0.95)

plot_coef_forest(
  results_df,
  term_col = "var_label",
  estimate_col = "estimate",
  low_col = "conf.low",
  high_col = "conf.high",
  p_col = "p.value",
  p_breaks = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2),
  p_labels = c("****", "***", "**", "*", ".", "ns"),
  facet_by = NULL,
  order_by = c("input", "estimate", "p"),
  x_label = NULL
)

tbl_coef_forest(
  results_df,
  term_col = "var_label",
  estimate_col = "estimate",
  low_col = "conf.low",
  high_col = "conf.high",
  p_col = "p.value",
  p_breaks = c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2),
  p_labels = c("****", "***", "**", "*", ".", "ns"),
  digits = 2
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

outcome, feature

Names of the outcome and the single predictor.

family

A [stats::family] object (default [stats::gaussian()]).

normalize

If `TRUE` (default) also fit on the 0..1 scaled predictor.

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

id_col

Name of the grouping (subject) column for the random intercept.

results_df

Results of [glm_single()], [lmm_single()] (stacked with `rbind()`/`dplyr::bind_rows()`), or any data frame with the columns named below.

term_col, estimate_col, low_col, high_col, p_col

Column names (defaults match `glm_single()`).

p_breaks

Increasing p-value cut-offs (default `c(0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2)`).

p_labels

Labels, one more than `p_breaks` (default `c("****", "***", "**", "*", ".", "ns")`). A p-value gets the label of the first break it is **strictly below**; p at or above the last break gets the last label; a missing p-value gets `""`.

facet_by

Optional column to facet by (for example `"scale"`).

order_by

`"input"` (default) keeps the row order, `"estimate"` and `"p"` sort.

x_label

Axis label (default: "Coefficient estimate with confidence interval").

digits

Decimals for the estimate and its interval.

Value

A tibble of class `cbe_coef_screen` with `feature`, `var_label`, `scale`, `term`, `estimate`, `std.error`, `statistic`, `p.value`, `conf.low`, `conf.high`, `n`, `status` (`"ok"` or a reason) and `warning`. One row per coefficient of the predictor (the intercept is omitted).

Scales

`scale = "raw"` is the change in the outcome (or in the log odds, log rate, ...) per **one unit** of the predictor. `scale = "normalized"` is the change across the **whole observed range** of the predictor (the predictor is min-max scaled to 0..1 with [min_max_norm()]), which makes coefficients of different predictors comparable in size. A non-numeric predictor has only the raw scale (its coefficients are the contrasts with the reference level).

Guards

A predictor with fewer than two distinct non-missing values, or an outcome with none, returns one row with `status` saying so instead of an error, so a screen over many predictors does not stop. A model that fails to fit also returns a row with the message; convergence or singular-fit warnings are kept in `warning`.

Intervals

For `glm_single()` with a family whose coefficient table is t-based (gaussian, quasi), the limits use the t quantile with the residual degrees of freedom, so the interval excludes 0 exactly when the p-value is below `1 - conf_level`; for z-based families (binomial, poisson) they use the normal quantile.

Mixed models

`lmm_single()` fits `outcome ~ feature + (1 | id_col)` with [lme4::lmer()] (maximum likelihood is not used for the fixed effects; REML). Confidence limits and p-values are **Wald** (normal approximation): `estimate +/- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * std.error` and `2 * pnorm(-abs(statistic))`. They are optimistic for small numbers of subjects; use `lmerTest` or a bootstrap ([boot_lmer()]) for small data. Rows with a missing outcome, predictor or id are dropped.

See also

[cox_single()], [batch_cox_single()], [plot_coef_forest()]

Examples

glm_single(mtcars, "mpg", "wt")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   feature var_label scale   term  estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low
#>   <chr>   <chr>     <chr>   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 wt      wt        raw     wt       -5.34     0.559     -9.56 1.29e-10    -6.49
#> 2 wt      wt        normal… wt      -20.9      2.19      -9.56 1.29e-10   -25.4 
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: conf.high <dbl>, n <int>, status <chr>, warning <chr>
glm_single(mtcars, "am", "wt", family = binomial())
#> # A tibble: 2 × 13
#>   feature var_label scale    term  estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low
#>   <chr>   <chr>     <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 wt      wt        raw      wt       -4.02      1.44     -2.80 0.00509    -6.84
#> 2 wt      wt        normali… wt      -15.7       5.62     -2.80 0.00509   -26.7 
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: conf.high <dbl>, n <int>, status <chr>, warning <chr>
